rules.title: By-value call arguments are moved
rules.statement: Passing an argument by value to a call moves it: each move-type l-value argument (and each owning `Box<dyn Trait>` binding consumed by a by-value parameter) is marked moved, suppressing scope-end auto-Drop on the caller's binding. Non-move-type / non-owning arguments are unaffected.

rules.title: By-value method receiver is moved
rules.statement: When the resolved method's formal `self` type is not a reference/pointer (kind not in {Ref, MutRef, Ptr}), the call consumes the receiver: the receiver l-value (move type or owning `Box<dyn Trait>`) is marked moved so scope-end auto-Drop does not double-free ownership transferred into the result. A `&self`/`&mut self`/`*self` receiver is not moved.

rules.title: Built-in slice/str length and pointer methods
rules.statement: On a slice receiver, `recv.len()` yields the element count as `i64`, and `recv.as_ptr()` yields the data pointer as `*const u8`. These are intrinsic (not user-resolved).

rules.title: &str.as_bytes() is the identity
rules.statement: Because `&str` is represented as `Slice<u8>` (same fat-pointer ABI as `&[u8]`), `s.as_bytes()` on a `Slice<u8>` receiver returns the receiver verbatim with no conversion.
rules.divergence: Logos models &str as Slice<u8> (writ/string-repr); identity conversion.

rules.title: &str methods forward to stdlib free functions
rules.statement: On a `Slice<u8>` (= `&str`) receiver, the methods {starts_with→str_starts_with, ends_with→str_ends_with, contains→str_contains, eq_str→str_eq, cmp→str_cmp, index_of→str_index_of, find→str_index_of, trim→str_trim, trim_start→str_trim_start, trim_end→str_trim_end, split→split} desugar to a call of the named stdlib free function with the receiver as the first argument, when that function exists.

rules.title: Method dispatch on slice/str impls
rules.statement: A method call on a slice receiver resolves user `impl Trait for [T]` / `impl Trait for str` methods via sentinel keys, in order: concrete `$slice$<elem>__<m>`, generic blanket `$slice$T__<m>`, and (for `Slice<u8>`) `str__<m>`. A `&[U]` argument whose formal parameter wants a flat `Slice` is reborrowed by stripping its `&`/`&mut` wrapper. If the receiver is a slice but no key matches, it is an error.

rules.title: Raw-pointer arithmetic methods require unsafe
rules.statement: On a raw-pointer (`Ptr`) receiver, the offset methods {add, sub, byte_add, byte_sub} and the distance methods {offset_from, byte_offset_from} are built-in, each require an `unsafe` context, take exactly one argument, and have result type: offset → the receiver pointer type (argument coerced to `i64`); distance → `i64` (argument must be a pointer).

rules.title: Raw-pointer is_null is safe; user impl wins
rules.statement: On a raw-pointer receiver, `p.is_null()` is safe (no dereference), takes zero arguments, and lowers to `(p as i64) == 0 : bool` — UNLESS the pointee type declares an inherent `is_null` method, in which case that user-defined method is dispatched instead.
rules.divergence: Logos lets an inherent fn on the pointee shadow the built-in pointer is_null.

rules.title: Tag-based dispatch on &tagged<TS> Trait
rules.statement: On a `TaggedPtr` receiver carrying tag-system TS and trait T, a method call resolves against T's declared methods (T must exist, method must exist), checks arg count = method param count − 1, requires `unsafe` if the method is unsafe, substitutes `Self`→receiver type in the return type, and emits a tag-dispatched method call (runtime type_code read via TS).

rules.title: Method call through &DstStruct requires unsafe unless self-describing
rules.statement: On a `DstRef` receiver of struct S, a method call dispatches `S__<m>` (concrete signature then generic). It requires an `unsafe` context unless S is `#[self_describing]` (tail length recovered in-band), in which case it is safe. No matching method is an error.

rules.title: Inherent impls on dyn override vtable dispatch
rules.statement: On a `dyn Trait` (or `&dyn Trait` / `&mut dyn Trait`) receiver, an inherent `impl Trait for dyn Foo` method (mangled `$dyn$Foo__<m>`) is tried before vtable dispatch; if found and applicable it is called directly rather than virtually.

rules.title: Virtual dispatch over the flattened supertrait vtable
rules.statement: Failing inherent resolution, a `dyn Trait` method call dispatches virtually: the method index is its slot in the supertrait-closure vtable layout (supertrait methods occupy real slots). Arg count must equal method params − 1, an unsafe method requires `unsafe`, and arguments are coerced to formal parameter types (arg-to-dyn, implicit reborrow, int widening) with type/variance/int-fit checks. Unknown method is an error.

rules.title: Self and trait args substituted in dyn return type
rules.statement: The return type of a virtual `dyn Trait` method is computed by substituting `Self`→receiver type plus the owning trait's type/const params from the TraitObject's trait args (read from the peeled `dyn` type, not from a `&dyn` reference whose own type_args are empty), so trait params do not leak unsubstituted to the call site.

rules.title: Method dispatch on tuple impls with autoref/autoderef
rules.statement: On a (possibly `&`/`&mut`-wrapped) tuple receiver of arity N, a method call resolves user `impl Trait for (T1..TN)` via keys concrete `$tuple$N$<t1>..$<tN>__<m>` then generic blanket `$tuple$N__<m>`, trying receiver shapes {Self, &Self, &mut Self}. The receiver is auto-referenced (mut per formal) when the formal `self` is a reference but the receiver is a value, or auto-dereferenced when the formal is by-value but the receiver is a reference. No match yields nullopt (falls through to standard diagnostics).
